perspectives.author: r/Mortgages
perspectives.title: Real affordability calculator
perspectives.snippet: Top comment · My mortgage is $1536. My property tax is $450 a month, and my insurance is $200 a month. That's putting me at $2186 already. Add utilities -- when I was renting, my utility bill was $25/month. At my house it's $200/month, with $400/month winters. We're at $2386 now. Maintenance, maybe $5k a year? I just got a 2-zone mini split installed due to my previous one breaking, and I need to cut down some large trees and replace my water heater. I DIY any repairs unrelated to plumbing/electricity, by the way, so if you have those done through a contractor it's even more expensive. So suddenly I'm around $2800. $1300 mortgage = probably $2400 housing expenses, if not more.
